text:
Alex Chen: heads-up — on customer alpha private deploy we saw a failed KMS decrypt during a canary rollout. requests started getting 500s.
Maria Gomez: do we have audit logs? which principal failed?
Alex Chen: root event id 4023456789 - svcacc 'redwood-inference-worker' trying to call keystore-proxy -> 403. quick splunk query i ran: `index=private_deploys source=keystore-proxy status=403 | stats count by service,src_ip`
Jordan Park: sounds like RBAC change — last week we tightened `svcacc` roles for staging. anybody remember removing `keystore.decrypt` from that binding?
Maria Gomez: also check netpol egress — if the proxy couldn't reach the HSM endpoint you'd also see failures. Can someone paste the netpol for keystore-proxy?
Alex Chen: pasting the minimal netpol we use in alpha for reference:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-keystore-egress
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-proxy
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          infra: kms
    ports:
    - port: 443
```
Lina Ortiz: if netpol blocked, proxy couldn't call HSM; RBAC 403 could be a token exchange failure on the proxy side (it returns 403 to the svcacc). check kube-audit for `TokenReview`/`SubjectAccessReview` events around the same ts.
ops-bot: (automated) alert: 4023456795 - KMS decrypt errors spike +30% in prod-private-region-2, grouped by keystore-proxy
Jordan Park: vuln triage note — matches the pattern where a mis-scoped role removal causes a graceful fallback to a legacy codepath that returns 403/500. we need to confirm whether any keys were attempted with a fallback key.
Alex Chen: checked: no outbound traffic to internet, all requests stayed internal between keystore-proxy -> kms-hsm. no evidence of exfil.
Maria Gomez: action items (short):
  1) rollback the role change for `redwood-inference-worker` svcacc on alpha (assigned @Jordan Park)
  2) add transient netpol egress allow for keystore-proxy -> kms namespace while we validate (assigned @Lina Ortiz)
  3) add an audit alert for keystore 403s > 10/min and tie to incident alert page (assigned @Alex Chen)
Jordan Park: starting rollback now, will post updates.
Jordan Park: rollback applied at 4023456808 — auth errors drop immediately. canary recovered.
Alex Chen: seeing successful decrypts after rollback, no more 5xx, canary passed :thumbsup:
Lina Ortiz: follow-ups for hardening:
  - add an integration test that exercises the keystore path under tightened RBAC during CI for private deployments
  - add a validation job that runs `kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:<ns>:redwood-inference-worker get secrets` (or a narrower `keystore:decrypt`) after role changes
Maria Gomez: draft of onprem playbook checks for customers:
```text
1) kubectl --context <customer> get networkpolicy -n infra -o yaml | grep allow-keystore-egress
2) validate egress to kms namespace (namespace label `infra: kms`)
3) run splunk: index=private_deploys keystore status=403 | stats count by service
4) check kube-audit for TokenReview/SubjectAccessReview events around the incident ts
```
Alex Chen: also request Console work: surface KMS client errors in per-route breakdown + include audit event id and direct link to logs. will help customers triage faster.
Maria Gomez: filing a vuln-triage ticket with timeline and customer impact, will tag `security-oncall`.
security-oncall: acknowledged, will pick up RCA and coordinate postmortem; please attach the splunk query + kube-audit snippet.
Alex Chen: thanks all — let's do a short retro tomorrow 11:00 to lock down the test + alerting changes and include checklist for private deploy docs.
